value.first: At 30 months she's in the sweet spot, so I'd start with the 3-Day Method. Skip it if she's constipated or a big change is landing. It works because diapers hide the feeling of being wet, and a few diaper-free days let a ready child link urge to action. Prep this week: pick 3 days at home, put a potty where you live, stock salty snacks and drinks she loves, and brief every adult.
value.second: Day 1: say goodbye to diapers, bare from the waist down, push fluids. When pee starts, carry her to the potty: "Pee goes in the potty." Prompt with "Tell me when you need to go." Accidents get the same flat line: "Pee goes in the potty. Let's clean up together." Day 2: after one success, a 20-40 minute outing, loose pants, no underwear. Day 3: a longer outing. Naps and nights stay in a pull-up.
value.third: Good signs: pees landing in the potty with prompting. Accidents for weeks are normal, and poop usually lags. If nothing lands by day 3 or she panics, go back to diapers and retry in 4-6 weeks. Call your doctor if she holds poop 3+ days or it hurts. If you can't clear 3 days, the gentler child-led way works too. I'll check in Thursday.
